findings.text: Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/catalog.mjs `providerOf()` labels any `anthropic/...` id "Claude (direct)", so the eval's `anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` row, which OpenRouter actually served, shows the wrong provider. It also shows up as a second Haiku row next to the hand-added "Claude Haiku" row. Label it OpenRouter, or merge the two rows into one.

The `z-ai/glm-5.3-flash:batch` row (models.json catalog) failed every call: OpenRouter returned HTTP 404 because a batch model can't use chat/completions. The grid still shows it as 0% / 0% / 0% in 0s, which reads as "this model is terrible". In `summarize()`, a run where every call errored should give null scores plus a "failed" marker, or the row should be left out.

The table the owner asked for is added at the very bottom of `render_models()` (public/framework/ai/overview.js ~line 419), below the whole existing value-per-kind analysis. So the main thing asked for is far below the fold. Per the presentation rule it should be the first thing on the Models tab, with the older analysis one click or one scroll down.
The notes heading says "Four things worth knowing" (overview.js render_catalog), but five bullets follow it.

There's no record of check_page at 400 or 1920, or of merge.mjs: task.jsonl ends at "session resumed" and the work sits as one commit on worktree/models-page. Requirement 4 hasn't been met yet. At 400 a 13-column grid needs a screenshot to prove it scrolls instead of overflowing the page.

The DataGrid builds a filter control for every `type: "number"` column, so this grid gets about 11 number-range filters above it. Setting `filter: false` on most columns, keeping only Provider and maybe Context, would make the page much easier to read.

The Claude prices and context windows are typed by hand in catalog.mjs (the `CLAUDE` const). The brief said prices are "computed ..., never typed". The code comment explains why (OpenRouter's short names point to a different model generation), which is reasonable, but the page should say so. The comment also gives no source for "200K for all three".

The Groq and Google AI Studio rows reuse OpenRouter's catalog price for that model id, not the price of the pinned provider, and their tokens in/out are blank because only eval-results.json was re-run. That's acceptable, but a reader will assume the price on those rows is Groq's or Google's.
The local rows have `context: null`, though the owner specifically asked to see context windows. The configured context size (the local server's settings) could fill them.

Servex/ext/openrouter/evals/catalog-price-snapshot.json adds a full ~2,800-line copy of OpenRouter's catalog to the repo. Saving only the ids the catalog actually uses would keep the diff, and every future refresh, small.
